entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Fulk of Neuilly was a French preacher of the 12th century who played a pivotal role in the Fourth Crusade.

As a prominent cleric, Fulk of Neuilly was instrumental in convincing the French nobility to support the crusade, which ultimately resulted in the sacking of Constantinople in 1204.

Fulk's actions not only had far-reaching consequences for the Eastern Orthodox Church but also left a lasting impact on the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the Latin and Byzantine empires.

His legacy as a key figure in the Fourth Crusade continues to be debated among historians, with some viewing him as a champion of Christian unity and others seeing him as a ruthless advocate for imperial expansion.

In the words of the 13th-century historian, Roger of Hoveden, 'Fulk of Neuilly was a man of great eloquence and persuasion, and his words had a profound effect on the minds of those who listened to him.'
